subject: Interruption advisory — partial generation failures and mitigation matrix (Velaris)
raw_messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Chen <evan@velaris.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Interruption advisory — partial generation failures and mitigation matrix (Velaris)

Hi Evan —

Wanted to notify you right away: since ~08:50 PT this morning we observed elevated error rates and partial generation failures affecting a subset of requests to our hosted inference API for your account (notably POST /v1/generate and streaming endpoints). Impact: ~7% of requests returned incomplete responses or 5xx before token completion, with P95 latency increasing from ~230ms to ~1.8s.

What we did immediately:
- Activated regional routing fallback to an alternate GPU pool to reduce tail failures.
- Temporarily enabled the model-variant fallback (quantized v2) for new requests to preserve throughput.
- Increased prefetch/caching headroom for your tenant to limit KV eviction.

Current status: the fallback routing reduced error rate to ~1.2% as of 09:05 PT, but some long-tail sessions may still observe truncations. We're continuing monitoring.

Short-term ask: if you see any ongoing customer-reported truncations, please forward example request IDs (x-request-id) and timestamps so we can correlate with the timeline.

We will follow up with a post-incident summary and a mitigations timeline. I’ve attached a brief timeline and a Grafana snapshot for your ops team. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts Velaris’ inference quality and are treating this as priority P1.

Sincerely,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Lead — Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20261205-incident-timeline-velaris.pdf
From: Evan Chen <evan@velaris.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:28:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Interruption advisory — partial generation failures and mitigation matrix (Velaris)

Thanks for the heads up, Sergio.

We started seeing a spike in incomplete completions in our production logs at 08:58; I’ve collected two representative request IDs: req_20261205_08_58_112 and req_20261205_09_02_347. Both truncated mid-response.

Two questions: 1) do you have an ETA on a permanent fix or playbook so we can communicate internally? 2) will this affect our SLA credit calculation if it persists beyond the hour?

— Evan
Ops Lead, Velaris AI

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Chen <evan@velaris.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:45:22 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Interruption advisory — partial generation failures and mitigation matrix (Velaris)

Team — forwarding Evan’s sample request IDs. He’s asked for an ETA and SLA implications. Please triage and prioritize correlation. Summary of suspected root cause: sudden prefetch eviction and backend batching pressure in primary pool leading to KV cache misses and partial generation aborts. For immediate remediation we activated fallback routing and a quantized variant; that reduced visible errors but does not fix the underlying cache/batching imbalance.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik: please pull logs for the two request IDs and run KV eviction correlation. Also verify whether the fallback model variant introduced any downstream latency regressions for Velaris.
- Marissa: coordinate Ops comms and confirm whether we should trigger a formal incident page update.
- Hannah: track customer messages and ensure we provide a short internal playbook for support to reference.

I’ll keep Evan on the thread for transparency.

— Sergio

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evan Chen <evan@velaris.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 11:07:41 -0800
Subject: Re: Interruption advisory — partial generation failures and mitigation matrix (Velaris)

Quick technical summary from triage:
- Correlated both request IDs; errors coincide with elevated KV cache eviction counts on the primary US-West pool between 08:46–09:08 PT. Evictions triggered a sequence where KV warm-up missed some attention keys and the runtime aborted generation for in-flight sessions.
- Root trigger appears to be an inefficient prefetch fanout during a short token-rate burst from a mixed-tenancy burst (unrelated customer workload spike).

Mitigations applied:
1) Regional fallback routing to an isolated pool (reduced multitenant contention).
2) Throttled large-prefix prefetches for that pool to avoid cascade eviction.
3) Hard limit placed on concurrent large-context sessions for your account to reduce edge cases while we stabilize.

Next steps / ETA:
- Short-term (0–6 hours): continue routing to isolated pool; monitor P95 and error-rate; expect full stabilization in 30–90 minutes as caches warm.
- Medium-term (24–72 hours): deploy a targeted prefetch backoff policy and an eviction-resistant LRU tweak to the runtime. Tentative deployment window tomorrow 02:00–04:00 PT.
- Long-term: we’ll add a tenant-aware prefetch throttle and an automated fallback activation rule for similar token-rate bursts.

On SLA: Marissa — please confirm, but we should prepare an incident record for evaluation against our SLA policy. I’ll annotate the causal vector so credits can be calculated if needed.

Attaching the Grafana snapshot and timeline Sergio included.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachment: grafana-p95-panel-screenshot.png
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Chen <evan@velaris.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: incident record and next steps (Velaris)

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for the quick examples. We’ve stood up an incident record and escalated this to P1. Short summary of actions and what to expect next:

- Current status: mitigations reduced visible impact; we anticipate continued normalization over the next 1–2 hours as caches warm fully.
- Post-incident deliverables we will share within 72 hours: a concise timeline, root cause analysis, concrete mitigations deployed, and a recommendation for any SLA credits.
- Planned fix: targeted prefetch backoff + eviction-resistant LRU change (planned rollout window tomorrow 02:00–04:00 PT).

If you’d like a dedicated 30-minute post-incident call with the engineering team, we can schedule one for tomorrow afternoon. Please let me know a preferred time.

We apologize for the interruption and appreciate your patience.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
